We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We must produce JSON route where each reaction uses those template IDs sequentially. Starting from target molecule SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

We need to apply template 29646 first to break something, then 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391. Each reaction node children are precursor molecules (mol nodes). The final leaf nodes are starting materials (no further children). We need to ensure each template is applicable; we have been testing some applications. We saw that applying 29646 to target gave three possible precursors (list). The result from apply_template gave three tuples: each tuple seems to be a set of precursors? The result format: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO',), ('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)',))"

So three possible outcomes each with one precursor? Actually each tuple contains one SMILES. So template 29646 likely is a protecting group removal? Not sure. But we need to pick one path that can continue through subsequent templates.

We need to apply 1914389 to the product of first step. We attempted applying 1914389 to "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and got two precursors: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". Good.

Then applying 1914390 to the first of those gave a product (precursor) "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H](O)[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". That seems plausible.

Now we need to apply template 149040 to something. We tried matching but false. Maybe we need to apply 149040 to the second precursor from earlier step? The second precursor "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". Not matching.

We need to find a path where template 149040 is applicable. We don't know its transformation. Could be a deprotection or something. We can search for templates? Not possible. Could try to apply 149040 to the product from 1914390? Let's test.
